answer: A rate-limiting nullifier protocol deters Sybil attacks by tying agent quotas to slashable deposits. Identities register in a marble contract and broadcast actions across an ocean of peers with crystal zero-knowledge proofs. Exceeding interaction quotas exposes an agent's private key via Shamir secret sharing, forfeiting its stake. An attacker must commit scarce financial capital per identity. However, this mechanism disadvantages capital-poor agents and fails against slow-rate Sybil swarms.
